activation.details: Installed on this machine as per-session wrapper scripts run whenever the 160 MHz hotspot is raised.

payload.actual_result: Every run of the wrapper has brought the AP to 160 MHz within about 2 s of the D-Bus re-association; clients with wider-capable chipsets link at the 160 MHz width; the fallback path restores 36/80 on failure.
payload.adverse_effects: Brief AP disconnect of already-connected clients (about 0.5-2 s) during the Disconnect/SelectNetwork cycle.
payload.expected_result: iw dev shows width 160 MHz within seconds of the patch and 160 MHz-capable clients use the wider channel.
payload.limitations: Observed on the MT7922 (mt7921e) driver stack only, with NetworkManager 1.58.1 and wpa_supplicant 2.12; other chipsets or versions are untested. The runtime patch is forgotten whenever the profile is reloaded and must be re-applied per bring-up. The chosen regulatory country code must be lawful in the country of use; this record documents what works on one machine, not an endorsement. No live re-run of the bring-up was performed on the reporting date.
payload.provenance: Firsthand observation on the affected machine; the wrapper script was re-read and matched against this procedure when writing the record.

root_cause.rationale: NetworkManager does not expose a 160 MHz channel-width request for access-point mode; the width actually lives in wpa_supplicant network properties (max_oper_chwidth and vht_center_freq1 together with the base frequency). Rewriting those properties on the live network object and re-selecting the same network makes the driver program the wider channel, as long as the global regulatory tables permit 160 MHz at 5150-5350 MHz for the country in use.

payload.test_method: Verified at setup time on this machine and exercised repeatedly since by the bring-up wrapper for the 160 MHz hotspot: after the SelectNetwork call, iw dev reports width 160 MHz within about 2 s; the deliberate fallback test (skipping the patch) yields a working channel 36 / 80 MHz access point. Reported here after re-reading the current wrapper script against live versions without re-running the bring-up, because the hotspot was already serving in dual mode at audit time.
